criteria.description: A standalone module importable as top-level `coverage_judge` (either a `coverage_judge.py` module or a `coverage_judge/` package — in both cases runnable later via `python -m coverage_judge`) is added to the voice-tutor repo, with a hermetic test file at tests/test_coverage_judge.py. The hermetic tests make NO network/LLM calls; no Anthropic client is constructed at import time, and none is constructed during the hermetic test run (the suite runs with no API key and no network). A lazily-defined, never-reached model-invocation seam (repo-standard, per claims.py) is permitted. Nothing reachable from the hermetic tests imports bot.py, the server, pipecat, or any live app path.
criteria.verifyBy: `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/test_coverage_judge.py -q` passes offline (no network, no API key set); `import coverage_judge` succeeds without constructing an Anthropic client; grep/AST confirms no import of bot/server/app/pipecat modules from the hermetic test path and no client construction at module import time.

criteria.description: Claim-list loading: a function loads a claim list into an ordered collection of claims each exposing an id and claim text, tolerant of the repo's actual .claims.json sidecar shape ({"claims":[{"id","claim",...}]}) — normalizing the `claim` field to text and accepting either the sidecar envelope or a bare list. Preserves input order and rejects an empty claim list.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic tests in tests/test_coverage_judge.py: load a well-formed sidecar-shaped structure (id + `claim`) and a bare list and assert ids+text extracted in order with `claim`→text normalization; assert a clear typed error is raised on empty claim list.

criteria.description: Claim-list validation surfaces clear, typed errors (module-defined exception, not bare KeyError/IndexError) on malformed input: missing id, missing/blank text, duplicate claim ids, and non-list/non-envelope top-level shape.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic tests assert the module's validation error type is raised with an informative message for each malformed case (missing id, missing text, duplicate id, wrong top-level type).

criteria.description: Transcript loading/validation: a function loads an indexed transcript as a list of turns each normalized to {index:int, role, content}, guaranteeing a stable integer index space so verdict `turns:[int]` can reference transcript indices. Rule: if NO turn carries an `index`, assign contiguous 0-based indices in list order; if indices ARE supplied, they must all be ints and unique and are preserved as-is. Malformed input (missing role/content, non-int supplied index, a partially-supplied index set where some turns have an index and some do not, duplicate supplied indices, non-list top-level) raises the module's typed validation error.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic tests: (a) load a transcript whose turns carry NO index and assert normalized turns are [{index:int, role, content}] with contiguous 0-based indices assigned in list order; (b) load a transcript with fully-supplied unique int indices and assert they are preserved as ints; (c) assert the module's validation error is raised for missing role/content, a non-int supplied index, a partially-supplied index set (some turns have index, some don't), a duplicate supplied index, and a non-list top-level.

criteria.description: Markdown-fence stripping: a pure function strips surrounding ```json / ``` fences (and plain ``` fences, with or without a language tag, with surrounding whitespace) from a model text response and returns the inner text (parsing is a separate step so the two functions compose cleanly), and is a no-op on already-clean JSON text.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic tests feed fenced (```json ... ```), plain-fenced, and unfenced strings and assert the parsed JSON value is equal in all cases (equality at the parsed-value level, not byte-identical text).

criteria.description: Strict verdict parsing produces, for a given claim-id set, a collection of verdict objects each of shape {claim_id, covered: bool, turns: [int]} with types validated (covered is bool, turns is a list of ints). An empty `turns` list ([]) is valid (e.g. a covered:false verdict): type validation checks list-of-int and emptiness is permitted, not an error. Malformed verdict entries (non-bool covered, missing fields, non-int turns element) raise the module's parse error.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic tests: a valid parsed payload yields correctly typed verdicts including a verdict with turns:[] accepted; payloads with a non-bool covered, a missing claim_id field, and a non-int turns element each raise the module's parse error.

criteria.description: Completeness/truncation detection uses a defined exception hierarchy: a single module-defined base parse error with distinguishable subclasses (or a typed discriminator attribute) covering (a) invalid JSON, (b) truncation/count-mismatch, (c) unknown/extra claim_id, (d) duplicate claim_id in output, and (e) missing claim_id. Verdict claim_ids must exactly match the input claim-id set. The count/completeness check is measured against the TOTAL claim count (every claim id must appear exactly once regardless of its covered value).
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic tests: a verdict list shorter than claim count raises the truncation/count-mismatch subclass; an unknown/extra claim_id, a duplicated claim_id, and a missing claim_id each raise their respective subclass — asserted via `isinstance(err, <NamedSubclass>)` and all being subclasses of the module's base parse error; a payload where all claim ids appear exactly once (mix of covered true/false) parses successfully.

criteria.description: Invalid JSON (non-JSON text after fence stripping) raises the module's defined parse-error base (or a subclass) rather than an unhandled json.JSONDecodeError, so callers/retry logic can catch a single defined exception type.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test feeds garbage/partial-JSON text and asserts `isinstance(err, <ModuleBaseParseError>)` is raised (not a raw json.JSONDecodeError).

scope.description: New files only within the voice-tutor repo (top-level `coverage_judge` module/package + tests/test_coverage_judge.py, matching the repo's flat top-level module style like claims.py/documents.py). Do NOT modify bot.py, the server, existing prompts, labels.json, claim maps, transcripts, or any live path under ~/.voice-tutor.

Sprint 0 is offline foundations only: no live Anthropic/model call implementation exercised, no fixtures copied yet, no credentialed smoke, and no app wiring/ledger writes. The actual judge invocation, v2 prompt hashing against fixtures, union_coverage, CLI, and credentialed label-agreement smoke belong to later sprints and are out of scope here.
Transport-defense parsing functions must be pure and model-independent (no Anthropic client dependency); any model-call surface must be injectable/mockable so hermetic tests stay network-free.

criteria.description: The module (top-level coverage_judge.py, a new file following the repo's flat top-level module convention) defines the v2 judge prompt as an in-module, embedded, versioned artifact: the full prompt text is loadable in-process via a stable module symbol/accessor (a module constant or packaged resource embedded in the source, NOT read from the external eval-set folder at runtime) and carries an explicit version identifier equal to 'v2'.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test in tests/test_coverage_judge.py imports the module and asserts the v2 prompt text is a non-empty str exposed via a stable symbol/accessor, that a version identifier equal to 'v2' is exposed alongside it, and — to prove embedding independent of any specific filesystem path — that the accessor still returns the same non-empty text when filesystem reads are monkeypatched to fail (e.g. builtins.open and pathlib.Path.read_text/read_bytes patched to raise), demonstrating no file I/O occurs at access time.

criteria.description: The module implements a deterministic prompt-hash function that reproduces the repo's exact v1 hashing scheme. The v1 prompt input used for verification is the byte-for-byte contents of judge-prompt-v1.md (embedded as a test fixture/constant, copied verbatim, not paraphrased or reformatted), and hashing that exact v1 text with the module's public hash function yields exactly the literal '632b73a34b1a22b1'.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test embeds the verbatim bytes of judge-prompt-v1.md as a fixture, hashes them with the module's public hash function, and asserts equality to the literal '632b73a34b1a22b1'; the test documents/asserts the fixture is the unmodified v1 text (byte length / content copied verbatim). Passes offline with no network.

criteria.description: The prompt-hash function is a genuine content-sensitive hash primitive (not a lookup table): it is pure and deterministic (same input always yields the same output across calls), maps different inputs to different outputs, is the single public function used to hash both v1 and v2, and produces a correct digest for arbitrary inputs — not only the two known prompt texts. The module documents (in source, e.g. docstring/comment) the concrete hash primitive it uses (algorithm plus any truncation/digest-size), and the SAME primitive that the function actually computes must be the one that reproduces the v1 target '632b73a34b1a22b1' in c2 (one hash function, cross-checked two ways — not independently guessable per criterion).
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test (a) calls the function twice on identical input and asserts equal outputs; (b) calls on two different inputs and asserts different outputs; (c) supplies an arbitrary third probe string chosen by the test and asserts the function returns a value matching ^[0-9a-f]{16}$ AND equal to a self-contained inline recomputation of the module's documented primitive over that same probe input — where the test writes the recomputation out explicitly (e.g. hashlib.sha256(probe.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:16], or hashlib.blake2b(probe.encode('utf-8'), digest_size=8).hexdigest(), matching whatever the module's source documents) rather than calling the module — proving it is a real hash rather than a hardcoded two-entry map; (d) the SAME inline recomputation primitive used in clause (c), applied to the verbatim v1 fixture from c2, must itself reproduce '632b73a34b1a22b1' (proving c2 and c3 test the one same primitive); and (e) confirms the same public function object is applied to both v1 and v2.

criteria.description: The module exposes the v2 prompt's hash computed via the same public scheme, derived from the v2 text at load time (not a hardcoded literal), in a form suitable for embedding into every verdict's metadata as judge_prompt_hash.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test asserts, using the module's OWN exposed accessors, that module's v2 hash accessor == module.hash_fn(module's v2 prompt text); that the value matches ^[0-9a-f]{16}$ (same shape as the v1 target literal); and that it differs from the v1 hash.

criteria.description: v2 is a strict tightening of v1, not a replacement that trades recall. v2 must (i) contain a named/labeled section that constrains coverage against topic/keyword/shape adjacency (the v1 strictness dimension — an explanation merely on the same topic or sharing keywords/shape is not automatically covered), AND (ii) contain a DISTINCT, separately-labeled content-match section requiring that 'covered' means the tutor's explanation is consistent with the claim's SPECIFIC assertions (same substance), enumerating the fluent-wrongness exclusions — an explanation that substitutes different list members, uses a different mechanism, or contradicts/substitutes specifics is NOT covered even if fluent and adjacent (targeting the c30 failure). v2 prompt text must not be byte-equal to v1.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test asserts, using deterministic literal string matching (case-insensitive) against the v2 prompt text: (a) the v2 text is NOT byte-for-byte equal to the embedded v1 text; (b) v2 contains two DISTINCT labeled section headings/markers — one adjacency-strictness section and one content-match section — detected as two separate literal heading tokens present in the text; (c) the v2 text literally contains a concrete marker token for EACH of the following fluent-wrongness anchors (one detectable substring per anchor, verified individually so a missing one fails): a 'list members' / 'different list members' anchor, a 'mechanism' / 'different mechanism' anchor, a 'contradict' or 'substitute' anchor for contradicted/substituted specifics, and an insufficiency anchor asserting same topic/keyword/shape/fluency alone is NOT sufficient (e.g. contains both an adjacency term — topic|keyword|shape|fluent — and a negation/insufficiency term — not|insufficient|alone); recall-retention is verified ONLY by asserting BOTH distinct labeled sections exist as separate headings — NOT by substring-matching the whole v1 text — so a verbatim v1 paste (which lacks the distinct content-match section and its anchors) fails, and a v1-stripped rewrite (which lacks the adjacency section) also fails.
